adopted.summary: Use two horizontally flowing diagrams stacked in the documentation: a container-level system topology and a component-level MCP distillation view. Generate both SVGs deterministically from one script.
adopted.rationale: Separating levels preserves ownership clarity while still exposing the MCP protocol, subagent roles, exact tool access, consent, validation, and write gates. External actors remain outside boundaries, GitHub owns durable review state, and the Review Assist Application owns webhook automation and guided review.

tour.title: Clarify system ownership and external actors
tour.what: Replaces the mixed narrative with a three-boundary topology: Developer machine, GitHub, and Review Assist Application, plus external Developer and Human Reviewer actors. The webhook, guided-review application, identities, and directional GitHub flows are explicit and vendor-neutral.
tour.why: A reviewer can now see who owns each behavior and where durable review state lives without inferring GitHub internals or confusing a human actor with an application component.
tour.attention: The Pull request box intentionally compresses the distinction between files in the head commit and the PR resource for container-level readability.

tour.title: Separate subagent orchestration from MCP enforcement
tour.what: Adds a dedicated MCP detail in which the calling agent runtime coordinates Author and Intent Reviewer subagents. Each calls a role-scoped MCP tool surface; the server performs deterministic consent, interview, validation, and local-write responsibilities without model calls.
tour.why: The earlier view made the MCP Server appear to host or spawn model-driven roles. The separation matches the transcript, generation guide, role templates, and REVIEW_ASSIST_ROLE tool registration.
tour.attention: The label “spawns · coordinates” describes caller behavior, not an in-repository scheduler.

tour.title: Make architecture artifacts reproducible
tour.what: Adds the docs:architecture npm script that regenerates both committed SVG files from the checked-in generator.
tour.why: The SVGs remain reviewable artifacts while their source, layout rules, palette, and accessibility metadata are deterministic and maintainable.
tour.attention: Regeneration is currently manual; this change does not add a CI drift check.
